name: Retreat House
character: Barn-wood hospitality: schedule-led, sleep-and-sew practical, generous type for a house full of quilters.

sections.eyebrow: A quilt retreat house in Amish country
sections.title: Bring a project and eleven friends
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: {{guild_name}} is a farmhouse and a converted dairy barn outside {{city}}, booked whole to quilt groups from Friday afternoon to Sunday supper.

items.title: Twelve stations
items.body: Eleven hundred square feet of six-foot tables, central pressing, and two big cutting mats.

items.title: Design walls
items.body: Flannel-covered, one across the barn gable and two more that live in the farmhouse hall.

items.title: Sleeps ten
items.body: Four bedrooms, real beds, and linen you do not have to pack.

items.title: A serious kitchen
items.body: Two ovens, a second fridge, and a list of local cooks who understand a six o'clock sewing deadline.

sections.heading: A barn, a farmhouse, and one bar of cell service on the porch rail
sections.html:
The barn milked cows until 1998 and held hay until 2019, when the last stall came out and the tables went in. It has a woodstove, a half bath, and lights that stay on as long as the sewing does. The farmhouse next door sleeps ten and holds the kitchen, the porch, and a hand-quilting frame that has never once stood empty.

Regulars call the weak cell signal a feature. The wifi reaches the barn, the coffee is on from six, and nobody has to be anywhere.

items.quote: We have held our fall retreat here three years running. The design walls stay up all weekend and nobody has to pack an iron.
items.author: Dana, retreat chair of a Columbus bee

items.quote: Eleven of us spread out like we were at home, and the coffee never ran out.
items.author: Marge, open-retreat regular

sections.title: The house and the barn
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: What is here, what it costs, and what to bring. The rest you will have figured out by Friday night.

items.title: The sewing hall
items.body: Twelve six-foot stations with task lighting, two pressing stations, and cutting mats that live in the middle of the room so nobody hoards them.

items.title: Bedrooms
items.body: Four bedrooms: two kings, four twins, and a daybed. Linen, towels, and a night light on the stairs.

items.title: The kitchen
items.body: Two ovens, a second refrigerator, dishwasher, and a long table that seats fourteen for supper.

items.title: Outside
items.body: A screen porch with the hand-quilting frame, a fire pit, and parking for twelve cars behind the barn.

items.title: Whole-house weekend
items.body: Friday at 4 pm to Sunday at 4 pm. Sleeps ten, sews twelve.

items.title: Weekdays
items.body: Monday morning to Thursday afternoon. Quiet, and the morning light in the barn is worth it.

items.title: Day retreat
items.body: Nine to nine, tables and kitchen, no beds. Good for shops and bee days.

items.title: Deposit
items.body: Holds the dates and applies to the balance. Refundable to sixty days out.

sections.heading: What is included
sections.html: Tables, chairs, pressing stations, design walls, wifi, coffee, tea, and the shelf of community rulers, mats, and the one purple thimble that has survived nine years. You bring your machine, your project, and your quorum. One well-behaved dog is negotiable.

sections.title: Open retreats
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: A few weekends each season the house opens by the seat. Bring yourself; leave with ten new addresses.

sections.heading: How an open weekend runs
sections.html: Doors open Friday at four and supper is at seven. Sewing goes as late as the barn lights do. Meals are simple and themed: soup night, taco night, leftover night. The show and tell after Sunday brunch is the real reason to come, and seats are $195 a person for the weekend, bedding included.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Two generations, one barn, and a hostess who will tell you where the good quilt shops are.

sections.heading: From dairy to design walls
sections.html:
The barn stored hay long after the cows left, and it took a decade of weekends to imagine it full of quilters instead. We host one group at a time, most weekends from September through May, and we live close enough to fix the wifi and far enough to stay out of the way.

Our favorite weekends end with a finished top laid across the porch rail for a photograph. Send us the picture; we keep a wall of them in the kitchen, and it is the first thing new groups ask about.

items.quote: By Sunday morning nobody wanted to leave, and the hostess had already marked the calendar for next year.
items.author: A guild officer from Akron

sections.title: Bring your group
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Send your dates and headcount. We reply within two days with availability, a rate, and directions that mention where the gravel starts.

items.a: Whole-house bookings are a two-night minimum. Day retreats can be a single day, any day of the week.
Three hundred dollars holds the dates and applies to the balance. It is refundable up to sixty days before check-in.
Yes. The kitchen binder lists four local cooks who work quilt weekends, or bring your own food and take the leftovers home.
Groups sign a simple use agreement. Guilds with event coverage can add the house to their certificate; we will send the wording.
